gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-epilogue: Gveret Levin has a hand-drawn, rope-bodied curve and a tall x-height. Epilogue, a sans-serif with a wire-like monoline skeleton and loose curves, wants a modest size and is better for quick bits of text.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-erode: Gveret Levin hand-draws its curves with a steady, drafting-pen line and a pronounced x-height, friendly from the first glance. One welcomes with friendly curves; Erode, a serif, rewards a brief read.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-fira-sans: Gveret Levin brings a hand-drawn, rope-bodied curve and a pronounced x-height, friendly and inviting. Fira Sans, a sans-serif with no thick-thin contrast and wide s curves, starts to wear over long paragraphs.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-public-sans: Rope-bodied, hand-drawn curves make Gveret Levin instantly friendly. Public Sans, a sans with hefty lowercase and broad open counters, grounds that handwriting and is built for quick reads.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-supreme: Friendly and wire-bent, Gveret Levin holds a constant thickness, while Supreme, a plain sans, sets a heavy-looking strip of text. Longer passages feel dense but open, best taken in modest portions.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-general-sans: Gveret Levin is friendly and hand-drawn, with rope-heavy curves and a pronounced x-height. General Sans, a plain sans with steady pressure and bends free of snags, carries on smoothly across paragraphs but is happiest in compact blocks.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-manrope: A rope-thick, hand-drawn curve and pronounced x-height make Gveret Levin inviting. Manrope, a plain sans with bright openings at every curve, keeps that warmth going, best across brief lines.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-montserrat: Gveret Levin is hand-drawn and friendly, its rope-heavy curves sitting on a pronounced x-height. Montserrat, a geometric sans-serif with oversized counters, glides along, though extended text is gentler in modest portions.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-satoshi: Gveret Levin draws friendly, hand-made curves with rope-like heft. Satoshi, a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and open e, shares that generosity and stays comfortable across modest amounts of text.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-switzer: Rope-heavy, hand-drawn curves give Gveret Levin its friendly, inviting character, with a pronounced x-height. And Switzer, a sans-serif of tubular, wire-like letters, keeps its tall waist line tidy over paragraphs, though brief lines suit it best.
